question: Can a second change alter receiver-own births? Does a first hearing survive at a distinct, earlier round?
reading: Compare the same history with and without its next single change. Strict own means ancestry from that end alone. Distinct receptions retain the first-only response at its first difference from the unmarked growth, and differ from first-only at a later round.
censoring: A missing difference is only through the last common round. The setting round plus the holder-step count plus one is a comparison benchmark.

design.targeted: Seven named cases. Change each linked strict far member with each sign after rounds 3, 1, 2. When heard, try both signs at each linked strict far member in the next six setting rounds and immediately after the first hearing and one round later, where the comparison reaches the setting. Read to round 18 or 10,000 knots.
design.longer check: For the four-knot far end with loose counts 1,1,1,2 and the other four-knot receiver with loose counts 3,2,2,2, the same tests from a first change after round 3 were read to round 32 or 10,000 knots.
design.broader: Equal weighting within each of four strata, seed 26112613. Up to 20 label pairs per stratum with an initial link, no link at round 16 and a baseline that completed round 16. Two strata use the switch as receiver, two use census receivers. Each is split by link present versus absent or missing at round 3. First changes after rounds 1 and 2, through round 16 or 10,000 knots.
design.higher caps: The matched switch receiver under caps five and six with the cyclic four-knot far end. First change after round 1, allowing an earlier arrival. Read to round 15 or 10,000 knots.
design.selection: The first two named starts have recorded first hearings. The panel includes shorter and longer surviving links, a far end whose own members are lost, an alternative receiving start, and the cap of four. Stop an exploratory panel on its first two separate strict-far receptions. The close-to-receiver, spent-site and waiting checks are controls.
